title: Clear the 17 SonarCloud code smells surfaced by the smoke-helper file split so the main Release Gate unblocks
goal: PR #373 moved 845 lines of long-lived helper code into frontend/tests/smoke/system/system-pages-helpers.ts. SonarCloud automatic analysis only raises issues on new code, so the move re-classified every line as new and surfaced 17 latent code smells (4x S7763, 1x S7503, 11x S9382, 1x S4043), all in that one file. The main-branch Release Gate blocks on any unresolved issue, so main is currently red. Fix the smells with behaviour-preserving edits: mechanical fixes where provably safe, NOSONAR with a written justification where the sequential await is intentional test-fixture semantics.
findings: SonarCloud automatic analysis raises issues only on code it has not analysed before; the same helper lines inside the old system-pages.spec.ts carried 0 issues across all analyses (verified via component-scoped issue search), while the identical code in the new helpers file raised 17.
The release-gate.yml 'Check unprocessed SonarCloud issues' step counts every unresolved issue on main (resolved=false, all types), so even MINOR code smells block a release.
All 17 findings are concentrated in one file, which makes a single focused commit the right fix shape.
4 of the findings (S7763) are pure import-plus-re-export barrels: converting to `export ... from` is provably behaviour-preserving.
1 finding (S7503) is an `async` keyword with no `await`; removing it keeps the returned Promise identical.
1 finding (S4043) is `targets.reverse()` used directly in `for...of`; hoisting the in-place reverse to a statement before the loop is behaviour-identical.

11 findings (S9382, await inside loop) are deliberate sequential semantics: children-first dept deletion order, per-item header fetching, ordered permission seeding and sequential auto-retrying assertions. Parallelising them would change fixture behaviour that the suite already validated in CI, so they are suppressed with `// NOSONAR` plus a written reason, following the existing repo convention (backend/pkg/testmysql/mysql.go, i18n_service_fast_test.go).

in: frontend/tests/smoke/system/system-pages-helpers.ts (S7763 export-from conversion, S7503 async removal, S4043 reverse hoist, 11x NOSONAR justification comments)
out: Any change to deletion ordering, header fetching cadence, assertion sequencing or fixture data
Parallelising the await-in-loop sites with Promise.all: it would change validated fixture semantics (e.g. dept children-first order) for no functional gain
Excluding tests/** from SonarCloud analysis: .sonarcloud.properties deliberately keeps tests fully analysed
Adding rule-level ignores to .sonarcloud.properties: SonarCloud automatic analysis does not support them (documented in that file for the i18n precedent)

acceptanceCriteria: All 4 S7763 findings are resolved by `export ... from` re-exports; the 4 symbols have no in-file usage other than the re-export (verified by grep before the edit).
waitForOkApiResponse no longer declares async but returns the same Promise<Response> value; all call sites keep working unchanged.
deleteDeptByName still deletes children before parents: the reverse() call happens before iteration, in place, on the same filtered array.
Every NOSONAR suppression carries a written justification and follows the repo's existing NOSONAR convention.
eslint passes on the modified file with zero warnings.
The smoke coverage contract still passes (34 smoke specs, 20 script entries) — the change adds no spec file and touches no script entry.
SonarCloud main analysis of the merge commit reports 0 unresolved issues and the Release Gate returns to green.

commands: grep -n for each of the 4 re-exported symbols in system-pages-helpers.ts (must show only the export-from lines)
SonarCloud main-branch issue search after merge: resolved=false total must be 0
runtimeEvidence: eslint clean output on the modified file
coverage-contract pass line (34 specs / 20 script entries)
SonarCloud issues API total before (17) and after (0) the fix

runtimeGap: Playwright cannot execute on this host (spawnSync EBUSY), so the modified helpers are not executed locally. Behaviour preservation is argued structurally (export-from is a rename-free re-export; async removal keeps the returned promise; reverse hoist is order-identical; NOSONAR adds comments only), and the executing proof is CI: the L1 tier plus module suites run the helpers against a real backend, and the SonarCloud re-analysis must report 0 unresolved issues.
